stance_text: Watch — unchanged in substance from the July Hold; the guide trim lowers near-term earnings but buybacks and acquisitions keep per-share growth intact
lens_text: FY2029 company-adjusted diluted EPS x exit P/E (three-year value); adjusted EPS adds back acquisition amortization (about $0.74 a year) and stock comp

bear.basis: FY2029 adj EPS $3.04 (FY2026 $2.95: Q4 adjusted EBITDA $150M, 19% below the guide-implied $184M; then 1%/yr) x 12x

base.basis: FY2029 adj EPS $3.59 (FY2026 $3.10, then 5%/yr: ~3% sales and ~2.5% share shrink, less a full year of higher interest) x 16x

bull.basis: FY2029 adj EPS $4.01 (FY2026 $3.10, then 9%/yr with acquisitions and margin recovery) x 19x

horizon_text: Fiscal 2029 (year ending early 2030) EPS at an exit P/E, undiscounted
thesis: Company-adjusted EPS compounds about 5% a year from ~3% sales growth (43rd percentile for its size) and ~2.5% annual share shrink, net of higher interest; the stock works at 15x adjusted EPS if margin holds near 12% EBITDA while acquisitions add volume.
consensus_view: The stock moved from $40.35 on October 9 to $47.44 on November 10 ahead of the print; the reaffirmed $950–980 million adjusted EBITDA guide was the company's stated expectation that the pre-announcement cut. No Street estimate snapshot was captured.
variant_view: At $47.44 the stock is 15.3x the low end of guide-implied FY2026 adjusted EPS ($3.10–3.15); this call holds that a 1% EBITDA trim does not change per-share growth of about 5% a year, so the multiple should hold unless the FY2027 guide shows EBITDA falling.

notes: The July call used one-year forward values on a Yahoo EPS estimate of unstated basis; this update uses three-year values on company-adjusted EPS, so the two fair values are not directly comparable.
No Street consensus snapshot and no peer multiples were captured for this update.
Revised twice after independent review: the first draft graded D, the second B; see review.

low_score_reasons: evidence: the second draft cited Q2's $32M interest as current although the Q3 pre-announcement shows $39M vs $30M; the bear's $2.95 anchor was not derived; 15.3x was computed on $3.10, not the $3.16–3.20 it was attributed to.

valuation: the 12x/16x/19x exit multiples carry over from a July call on a different EPS basis and are defended only by bracketing today's multiple; the 25/50/25 weights rested on one sentence; the base drivers compounded to under 5.6%, not 6%.
variant_view: with no consensus captured, the view is a hold-the-multiple position rather than a disagreement with an evidenced market belief, and the 15.3x price already agrees with it.
review.counter_case: Per-share growth is being bought with borrowed money, and the call's own interest-expense signal has already fired: Q3 interest expense was $39M against $30M a year earlier while adjusted EBITDA fell 1%, after H1 issued $929M of debt and repaid $617M while buying back stock. If FY2027 adjusted EBITDA is flat, a full year of higher interest offsets the share shrink and adjusted EPS stalls near $3.10; at 13–14x for a distributor whose margin has fallen and whose guide was just cut, that is about $40–43, below $47.44. On GAAP EPS (about $2.40) the stock already trades near 20x.
review.response: Accepted the interest finding (the author had misread the Q3 table). Changes: FY2026 anchor re-derived with Q3's $39M interest (guide implies $3.10–3.15, anchor at the low end); base growth cut from 6% to 5% a year to match its own drivers after the interest step-up; bull from 10% to 9%; weights moved from 25/50/25 to 30/50/20 because a pre-mortem signal has fired; the bear anchor now comes from an explicit Q4 EBITDA miss; the unsupported claim about how peers are valued was removed. Fair value fell from $58.25 to $54.91 (+5.0% a year), still Watch. Not changed: the exit multiples, because no peer or history data was captured to move them; the counter-case's $40–43 outcome is close to the bear case and carries 30% weight. The first draft was graded D (evidence 1) for an unsourced $2.75 EPS anchor.
